This primitive formalizes the additive scaling law: total habit strength equals the product of the number of reinforcement units and the efficacy of each individual unit. In adversarial settings, such as sports betting markets, this scaling law informs optimal resource allocation—overspending on reinforcement (e.g., excessively large bets) can paradoxically weaken learned strategies due to overfitting to high-variance outcomes.
